A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DetAny3D in Detect Anything 3D in the Wild. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary sections support reliable comparison across all 15 pages of v2 and 16 pages of v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original zero-shot and in-domain detection experiments, component and backbone ablations, prompt comparisons, and qualitative applications in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds training-data ablation results, inference-speed measurements, and per-category detection results in Tables 6–8.

M1.justification: The SAM/DINO architecture, 2D Aggregator, 3D Interpreter, zero-initialized ZEM layers, losses, and prompt-processing procedures remain unchanged. Revising ZEM's stated purpose from preventing forgetting to stabilizing training does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: DA3D's constituent datasets and the existing novel-category, novel-camera, in-domain, and qualitative application coverage are retained. The added appendix analyses use previously covered datasets and classes; the Omni3D-only training control introduces no new data domain or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding existing experiments is unchanged. The new appendix comparisons reuse Cube R-CNN and OVMono3D; no new external comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: V3 introduces an Omni3D-only versus DA3D training-data control in Table 6 and a KITTI inference-throughput evaluation using FPS in Table 7. Existing splits, AP metrics, prompt settings, model configurations, and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 9.3–9.5 substantially broaden the diagnostic evaluation: Table 6 tests the contribution of additional DA3D training data, Table 7 examines inference efficiency, and Table 8 exposes category-level strengths and weaknesses with easy/hard summaries. These address questions beyond the retained component, prompt, and backbone ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, while Tables 6–8 substantially expand the findings. New results include Omni3D-only DetAny3D at 24.33 AP versus the retained DA3D result of 24.92, throughput of 1.5 FPS versus OVMono3D's 7.1 and Cube R-CNN's 33.3, and per-category AP showing both gains and losses. These are additional measurements, not a same-setting improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and the supplementary camera-ray, embedding, and prediction definitions are retained. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised; the ZEM revisions concern explanatory claims.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine ZEM's contribution from mitigating catastrophic forgetting to stabilizing early 2D-to-3D transfer. The broader detection, generalization, and application claims remain unchanged. The stronger forgetting language still appears in Figure 2 and Section 3.3.

C2.justification: New Section 10 materially expands applicability boundaries: text-to-box prompting can lose semantic information and inherit occlusion failures; slow inference limits real-time robotics and driving; and single-frame processing omits temporal cues. Section 9.3 also attributes DA3D's principal benefit to novel-camera generalization. These extend v2's existing discussion of prompt bottlenecks and intrinsic dependence.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 removes the explicit statement that both methods in the qualitative comparison use text prompts with Grounding DINO. This slightly reduces experiment-specific documentation without establishing a changed procedure. Training hardware, hyperparameters, model implementation details, and repository access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 86 cited works and the same substantive related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Reference differences concern formatting and citation page pointers.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted ZEM wording revisions, compresses passages in Sections 4.2–4.5, clarifies supplementary cross-references, and updates author-contribution and funding text. It adds Sections 9.3–9.5 and a limitations section while retaining the overall narrative and organization.

P2.justification: V3 adds supplementary Tables 6–8 while retaining Figures 1–9 and the existing table structures. Local text reflow moves the conclusion onto PDF page 8, and supplementary pagination becomes continuous. The document is not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: V3 improves the paper's evidential transparency: Table 6 tests dependence on additional training data, Table 8 reveals uneven category performance, and Table 7 with Section 10 makes deployment costs and failure conditions explicit. These provide useful, bounded gains over v2. Timing conditions remain underspecified, and the revised ZEM claim still coexists with stronger forgetting language in Figure 2 and Section 3.3.
